headline: Carried-interest markdowns swing Carlyle to a net loss
summary_short: Carlyle's Q1 2026 GAAP revenue fell to $254M (-74% y/y, -75% q/q) as performance allocations reversed to a $681.1M loss, driving a net loss attributable to Carlyle of $132.2M (vs $130.0M net income a year earlier) and diluted EPS of -$0.37.
summary_long: The $132.2M net loss (vs $130.0M income a year earlier) was driven almost entirely by non-cash performance-allocation markdowns: Global Private Equity allocations reversed on CP VII depreciation from lower public-market marks and the preferred-return impact, partly offset by gains in international energy funds and CJP IV. Compensation fell in lockstep since performance-allocation-linked pay tracks the carry swing. Principal investment income rebounded because Q1 2025 carried a one-time NGP impairment and carry reduction from a strategic-investment restructuring that did not recur this year. Segment-basis Fee Related Earnings of $300.0M and Distributable Earnings of $327.0M held up far better than GAAP results. The Board held the dividend at $0.35/share and continued buybacks of $65.0M. No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: GAAP results swung to a loss almost entirely on non-cash performance-allocation mark-to-market reversals in Global Private Equity, not a decline in the underlying fee-based asset-management business.

Fund management fees were roughly flat; the revenue decline was driven by performance allocations swinging to a $(681.1)M loss, primarily depreciation in CP VII from lower public investment marks and preferred-return impact.
Tracks the performance-allocation reversal; partially offset by a $539.3M drop in performance-allocation-linked compensation, since that expense line moves with the same carry marks.
